personas.name: Tammy
personas.situation: PE teacher, now teaching Year 8 maths
personas.situationText: I'm a PE and health teacher. Because of a gap in the timetable I'm now teaching two Year 8 maths classes. I teach three days a week and I'm happy to put time in on my days off.

personas.name: Sam
personas.situationText: I'm in my second year, teaching Year 7 and Year 9 maths at a regional high school in NSW. I'm fine with the maths itself. My Year 9 class takes ages to settle and I lose the first ten minutes most lessons. In Year 7 the range is huge: some kids are still unsure of times tables and others finish everything in five minutes.

cachedDiagnosis.summary: Your maths is strong. What's hard is getting Year 9 settled quickly and pitching Year 7 work for a very wide range of students. You have about an hour and a half a week for learning.

needs.topic: Entry routines that get a class working in the first two minutes
needs.evidence: You said you "lose the first ten minutes most lessons" with Year 9.

needs.topic: One maths task, three entry points
needs.evidence: You said the range in Year 7 is "huge".
A clear "I do, we do, you do" structure helps both settling and differentiation.
Students who finish in five minutes need feedback that gives them somewhere to go next.
You're at a regional high school in NSW.
